title: Fit the blue suction-cup tool to a robot's manual quick-change flange and lock it on
instruction: Fit the blue suction-cup tool to the robot's tool flange and lock it on, leaving the gripper tool in the rack. Then let go of everything, with the tool hanging locked on the robot, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Robot cells swap end effectors (grippers, suction cups, welding torches) on quick-change tool changers. When a technician changes a tool by hand, on a manual changer or while recovering a cell after a fault, the new tool has to be held up square against the robot's flange while a locking ring or lever is turned; let go too early and the tool drops, damaging it or the fixture. One hand holds the tool, the other works the lock.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A robot arm of cast aluminium, fixed (switched off), its base 56 cm forward and 11 cm left of the centre line; its wrist reaches in low, ending in a steel tool flange 6.4 cm across whose face, 2 cm left of the centre line, looks to the right; the flange's axis is 30 cm forward and 8.5 cm above the table. A light on top of the wrist shows red. (2) A steel locking ring 8.8 cm across and 1.8 cm deep round the flange, just behind its face, with an orange-painted steel lever reaching 11 cm toward the arms and then bending to the left to a black rubber pad 4.5 by 3 cm (its middle 19 cm forward, 8.3 cm left of the centre line, its top 9.9 cm above the table, with a small lip on its near end). Pressing the pad down turns the ring (up to 35 degrees, about 0.1 N m or 1 N on the pad); a friction detent keeps it where it is left. (3) An aluminium tool rack right of the centre line with two slots, each tool lying along the left-right line, its plate facing left toward the flange: a blue suction-cup tool (120 g; a steel plate 6 cm across, its face 30 cm forward and 12 cm right of the centre line; a blue anodised-aluminium body 4.4 cm thick ending in a black nitrile-rubber suction cup 22.5 cm right of the centre line), and the robot's grey aluminium two-finger gripper tool (140 g), the same but 18 cm forward. Each tool has a square steel handle 1.6 cm across on top, 5 cm from its plate's face, its top 14 cm above the table. A tool is seated when its plate's face is within 6 mm of the flange's face, its middle within 1 cm of the flange's axis, its axis within 12 degrees of the flange's and its handle up (within 20 degrees). A tool seated while the ring is within 8 degrees of open is locked on once the ring is turned 25 degrees: it is drawn square onto the flange and the light turns green; turning the ring back below 15 degrees unlocks it. A ring turned with no tool seated locks nothing. Real build (a manual changer of the locking-ring type, sized for small arms): the robot side is a 64 mm steel flange (ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 mounting) with two 6 mm locating dowels in its face; the ring carries three internal cam lugs at 120 degrees that, turned 25 degrees, hook three lugs on the tool plate's rim and draw the plate onto the face; each tool side is a 60 mm, 8 mm thick steel plate with the three lugs and two 6 mm holes for the dowels. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 0.0 if the gripper tool was ever locked on. Otherwise 1.0: the suction tool locked on, each gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) at least 4 cm from its handle and from the lever's pad, and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the suction tool locked on otherwise; 0.25: the suction tool seated on the flange, with the ring open, at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the suction tool still.
reset_notes: Turn the ring back open, take the suction tool off and lay both tools back in the rack.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) at real size and mass. Simplified: the robot is fixed; its flange has no dowels and the ring and plate no cam lugs: seating is checked by pose (face within 6 mm, middle within 1 cm, axis within 12 degrees) and the lock is a fixed joint switched on when the ring turns 25 degrees with a tool seated; the ring's friction detent is a hinge spring moved to where the ring is left. Cameras 1280 x 704.
